oral-hygiene-for-scent.text: Users practise tongue cleaning and mouth care so breath does not detract from their overall scent when talking at close range. Most genuine bad breath is traced to oral bacteria, and the evidence for specific interventions is tentative.

pheromone-sprays-human-pheromone-science.text: Pheromone sprays are sold as fragrances containing human sex pheromones, and buyers use them hoping to raise their attractiveness to others. Peer-reviewed research has not shown that human pheromones change behavior, so the attraction effect rests on marketing and anecdote.

chain: Sweat steroid or fatty acid exposure
androstadienone-copulins-claims.text: Forum posters and product sellers cite androstadienone and copulins as human attraction chemicals that could make someone more appealing. Lab studies report small mood effects, while behavior change toward the wearer has not been shown.

natural-musk-and-scent-on-skin-theory.text: Proponents in appearance communities argue that a person's own body scent is part of attractiveness, and that perfumes and deodorants can mask or enhance it. General odor research exists, but the looksmaxxing claim itself is untested.

unscented-products-for-natural-scent.text: Users choose unscented soaps, deodorants and lotions so their skin scent is not mixed with or overwhelmed by cologne. The attraction benefit is untested, though fragrance-free products are documented as a choice for people with fragrance allergies.

chain: Different contrast with skin and eyes
hair-dye-bleaching.text: Users bleach hair lighter or dye it darker to change contrast with their skin and eyes, and to cover gray. The color change is immediately visible, and hair coloring is a well-established cosmetic method used by a large share of adults.

wardrobe-capsule-minimalist-wardrobe.text: Users build a small set of interchangeable, well-fitting staples so that every outfit looks coordinated. The better-dressed look is visible on the day it is worn, and it is a long-standing fashion idea rather than something tested in attractiveness studies.

old-money-quiet-luxury-style.text: Followers dress in understated, high-quality, tailored pieces with no visible logos to project discreet wealth and polish. The change in presentation is visible immediately, and the aesthetic is popular with no attractiveness studies behind it.

streetwear-techwear-style.text: Users dress in hip-hop, skate and outdoor-gear-derived clothing to look current and part of a style scene. The look is visible as soon as it is worn, and it is a style choice with no studies on attractiveness effects.

preppy-ivy-style.text: Users adopt Ivy League campus dress such as oxford shirts, chinos and loafers for a neat, classic look. The change in presentation is immediately visible, and it is a style tradition rather than something tested for attractiveness.

fit-focused-dressing-for-body-type-shoul.text: Users pick garment cuts that emphasise wide shoulders and a narrow waist so the torso reads as a V-taper. The visual change is apparent when the clothes are worn, and the approach is popular in style advice without clothing-specific trials.

vertical-stripes-monochrome-elongation.text: Style advice holds that vertical stripes and single-color outfits make a person look taller and slimmer. The underlying visual illusion has been studied, with mixed results, and the small perception literature points the other way for stripes.

chain: Camera angle, distance and lens chosen
photo-angle-maxxing.text: Users test camera angle, subject distance, lens and head tilt to find the framing in which they photograph best. The change in the resulting image is immediately visible, and the lens-distance physics is documented, while attractiveness effects are untested.

chain: Nose and face look more proportionate
camera-lens-distortion-portrait-lens-85m.text: Users shoot with a longer portrait lens from farther back so features nearest the camera, especially the nose, look less enlarged. The perspective effect is visible in the image itself, and the optics are well documented.

photo-lighting-golden-hour.text: Users shoot in golden hour or similarly soft light so faces show lower contrast and gentler shadows. The lighting difference is visible in the photo, and the physics is clear, while the attractiveness payoff has not been tested.

dating-profile-photo-optimization.text: Users pick and order dating-app photos using feedback from tools such as Photofeeler, where anonymous voters rate images. Popular in looksmaxxing circles, it has had little independent testing, and posters note that top-rated photos do not always perform best on apps.

chain: Scores show how strangers perceive you
photofeeler-testing.text: Users upload photos to Photofeeler to see attractiveness, trustworthiness and smartness scores from strangers, and treat it as a looks scoreboard. Its real-world meaning is disputed, with claims that voters favor smiling photos and scores may not match dating-app results.

glasses-frame-selection-by-face-shape.text: Users choose frame shapes to balance or complement their face, for example aiming for a hunter-eyes look. The frames visibly change the face's appearance once worn, and the face-shape pairing rules are widely repeated styling advice without testing.

chain: Eye bags, asymmetry or nose less prominent
glasses-to-mask-facial-flaws.text: Users wear chunky frames to draw attention away from features they dislike, such as eye bags, asymmetry or the nose. The frames are visibly present and change what stands out on the face, and the technique is a styling trick with no research behind it.

colored-lenses-blue-light-glasses.text: Users wear blue-light or tinted glasses for screen eye strain and, in some looksmaxxing circles, to reduce puffiness around the eyes. The puffiness link is anecdotal, and the eye-care bodies cited by Wikipedia do not recommend them for strain.

skin-tone-matching-foundation-bb-cream-f.text: Men use a light foundation or BB cream matched to their skin to even out tone and hide redness and marks. The evening-out is visible while worn, and a well-matched shade is described as hard to detect, though research on male appearance outcomes is limited.

chain: Darker shade in hollows, lighter on edges
Shadow and light change the face
men-s-makeup-contour-bronzer-highlight.text: Users apply subtle contour, highlighter and bronzer to make the jaw, cheekbones and nose look more defined. The shading effect is visible while worn and follows standard makeup practice, though male attractiveness has not been studied.

lip-balm-tinted-lip-color.text: Users apply lip balm, sometimes tinted, to keep lips smooth and add a natural shade. The moisturized, more even look is visible after application, and appearance research specific to lip balm is limited.

teeth-whitening-before-photos.text: Users time strips, trays or in-office whitening shortly before a photo shoot or event to brighten their smile. The shade change is visible and measurable on the day, with effects fading over time.

undercut-fade-with-textured-top.text: Users get short faded sides with a longer, styled top, which is widely recommended for many face shapes, and a skin fade is said to make the face and jaw look sharper. The haircut change is immediately visible, and its popularity is documented while attractiveness effects are unstudied.

buzz-cut-for-thinning-hair.text: Users with thinning or receding hair clip it very short to reduce the contrast between sparse and dense areas. The resulting look is immediately visible, and research on how shaved and bald looks are perceived is mixed.

chain: Jaw and forehead look more balanced
hair-length-for-face-shape-long-hair-max.text: Users match hair length and shape to their face, or grow hair longer under labels such as long hair maxxing, to frame features. The change in outline is visible as the hair grows or is styled, and the idea is popular advice without dedicated trials.

chain: Beard grown along jaw and chin
facial-hair-as-camouflage-weak-chin.text: Users grow a beard to add apparent projection and definition to a recessed chin or weak jawline. The visual change is plain once the beard fills in, and the practice is widespread although no study has tested the camouflage claim itself.

posture-awareness.text: Users practise noticing and correcting how they stand and sit, countering the head-forward posture of phone and desk use, to look taller and more present. The change in stance is visible while it is held, and posture research has focused on pain rather than attractiveness.

chain: Open stance, eye contact, slower pace
body-language-presence-training.text: Users train open stance, steady eye contact and slower movement to come across as more confident, often alongside posture and grooming. The research supports increased felt confidence more than measured outcomes in how others judge the person.
